institution: National Centre for Disease Control, National AMR Surveillance Network (NARS-Net)
citation: National Centre for Disease Control. AMR Annual Report 2020: National Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Network (NARS-Net India), reporting period January to December 2019. New Delhi: National Programme on AMR Containment, NCDC, Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; 2020.
reporting: Number tested, number resistant and percent resistant (%R), by pathogen for all specimens together and by specimen type (blood; pus aspirates with other sterile body fluids together, PA+OSBF; urine), all location types combined; location-type charts (inpatient, outpatient, ICU) with printed data labels for blood (S. aureus, E. coli, Klebsiella), PA+OSBF (S. aureus), blood with PA+OSBF and urine (Enterococcus) and all specimens (E. coli, Klebsiella, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter), with isolate numbers per location in the legends.
method: WHONET; first isolate of a priority pathogen per patient and specimen type (78,860 isolates reported, 74,200 unique patient isolates analysed); Enterobacteriaceae by Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion (two sites also automated identification and AST); colistin by broth microdilution per CLSI M02 and M100 for a limited number of isolates; breakpoint edition not stated; no vancomycin broth microdilution results for S. aureus.

verification.note: Tables 4 to 10 parsed from the PDF text layer (PyMuPDF words assigned to the number tested, number resistant and %R columns of each specimen group by their right edges; multi-line drug names joined) and every value then compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 2.2 to 2.6 (tables cropped). Every printed %R was recomputed from its printed counts (all agree within rounding) and every all-specimen column compared with the sum of its specimen columns. Table 2 counts transcribed from the text layer, compared with the page and checked against the column totals (16,189 blood, 33,642 urine, 24,368 PA+OSBF; 74,200 with the one stool isolate). Location charts (Figures 9 to 16, 19 and 20, vector horizontal clustered bars): each data label matched to its bar from the PDF drawing (label beside the bar end, bar colour to the legend marker), the bar length converted to a value with the axis ticks (every label within 0.1 of its bar), bars not drawn (0) placed by their position in the group; every chart then checked by eye on the rendered page, including the colour order (inpatient, outpatient, ICU from the top). Figures 17 and 18 read the same way and compared with Tables 6 and 7. Page numbers are PDF page numbers (1-based).

notes: Third NARS-Net annual report (titled AMR Annual report 2020): 21 medical college laboratories in 19 states reporting, seven priority bacterial pathogens, January to December 2019. All figures are percent resistant as printed (intermediate counted as not resistant). Specimens: this report gives pus aspirates and other sterile body fluids together (PA+OSBF), shown here under deep infections; the all-specimen columns ("Blood + Urine + PA + OSBF") are shown as all specimens, and the S. aureus "Blood + PA + OSBF" column as all specimens except urine (S. aureus is not collected from urine, so for it this is every specimen under surveillance). NARS-Net does not collect respiratory specimens. Table rows combine all location types (set all). Location rows (ward = inpatients, outpatients, ICU) come from bar charts with printed data labels and isolate numbers in the legends; the Enterococcus chart for blood with PA and OSBF is recorded as all specimens except urine. In the all-specimen columns the numbers tested equal the sum of the specimen columns (where every specimen is printed) but the numbers resistant differ slightly; only Pseudomonas ciprofloxacin differs beyond rounding (conflict). Figures 17 and 18 (E. coli and Klebsiella in urine and blood) contradict Tables 6 and 7 for several drugs: recorded as conflicts on the table rows. Only S. Typhi has percentages for Salmonella. Grey table cells are absent. No fungal data in this edition.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: the seeded sample of 113 of 453 cells (every table and chart), every row n and every count were read from the page images (scale 3, tables and charts cropped) and written down before comparing; every other cell was then read as well: all 453 cells, all 204 numbers tested, all 54 row n and all 19 counts (Table 2 on page 19 and the stool S. Typhi isolate on page 37). 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected. The validator's caution list prints the values of its 11 caution cells, so the one of them in the sample (E. coli blood ciprofloxacin) was not read blind; it was confirmed on the page.

Location charts (Figures 9 to 16, 19 and 20): each label checked against its bar (bar colour to the legend swatch, bars ordered inpatient, outpatient, ICU from the top, bar end at the label's value), organism and specimen from the chart title. The legend N of the all-specimen charts (Figures 14, 15, 19, 20) equal the ICU, IPD and OPD columns of Table 3, so Inpatient is non-ICU inpatients (ward). No setting, specimen or organism swaps.

All 11 cautions confirmed as printed (source inconsistencies, not transcription errors): Figure 17 (urine) labels E. coli ciprofloxacin 72 and Klebsiella ciprofloxacin 58, cefepime 34 and colistin 2 where Tables 6 and 7 print 79, 68, 64 and 3; Figure 18 (blood) labels E. coli ciprofloxacin 60 and Klebsiella ciprofloxacin 56 and colistin 2.6 where the tables print 72, 74 and 3.5 (each table value fits its own counts, and the Figure 13 and 16 location labels fit the tables); Table 9 Pseudomonas ciprofloxacin: the all-specimen column prints 3,517 resistant of 6,537 (54%) while its PA+OSBF, blood and urine columns (1,529 of 3,140, 321 of 1,006, 1,427 of 2,391) add up to 3,277 of 6,537 (50%); the Figure 19 labels (55, 49, 61, weighted 53.7) and the text (page 37) fit 54%.

Also confirmed: the 1 point Klebsiella ertapenem chart differences kept as per-drug notes (Figure 17 urine 47 against Table 7 48, 803 of 1,690 = 47.5%; Figure 18 blood 68 against 69, 572 of 835 = 68.5%). Every printed %R of Tables 4 to 10 recomputed from its printed counts: all within rounding (five cells at x.49 printed up, for example S. aureus blood gentamicin 1,163 of 4,390 = 26.49, printed 27); no further conflicts.
